raw_response:
I’m 48 this year, and I’ve worked these fields a long time. For my land, I’ll still do wheat and maize on all 30.4 mu. That’s the safest way for me. Wheat-maize is what we know here, and with some family working off-farm, I can’t manage anything too fussy. I have well water, so if the rain is short I can still protect the crop, but pumping costs money, so I won’t water too many times unless the crop really needs it. For wheat, I’ll sow in early October like usual, use a local improved variety that people around here trust, put most fertilizer at planting, then add some more at jointing if the seedlings don’t look strong enough. I’d rather not cut fertilizer too much because if wheat goes yellow, yield drops fast. For maize, after wheat harvest I’ll plant quickly in mid-June, no delay, because that window is short. I’ll use hybrid maize seed, put fertilizer once at planting and once later around the big bell stage if the stand looks good. I won’t spend too much on pesticide unless I actually see problems. What matters most for me is steady yield and not running short of cash.
